match_id: Crystal Palace_GLASNER: “IT WOULDNT BE THE BEST FOR FOOTBALL!”  Liverpool_2026-04-25_bUbD2kdfG-8
opponent: GLASNER: “IT WOULDNT BE THE BEST FOR FOOTBALL!”  Liverpool
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Okay, who would like to start, please? Matt.  Thank you. A very open game. It felt like we have  
seen that game quite a lot this season, with  the missed chances and being punished. But how  
do you see the game? Are you pleased with the  performance overall? Yes, absolutely. We are  
very disappointed about the result, yes, but  we are very pleased with our performance.  
I think it was our best performance here at  Anfield, even when we lost the game. But yeah,  
created so many chances. But today, I think the  difference was the efficiency, and Liverpool  
took their half-chances and we missed our big  chances. So that is maybe the summary. And I just  
talked to the players because they were really  disappointed. It was a huge effort again.  
And then I showed them the stats, you know, we  are having 14 to 9 finishes here and an xG of  
2.3 to 0.9. That is just amazing, and it shows  how competitive we have been. And this gives us,  
or should give us, a lot of confidence for  the final part of the season. And what I  
liked most, and credit to the  players, is 2-0 down at half-time,  
they could also think, in five days we play  the Conference League semi-final, let’s  
rest a little bit of power for Thursday. But it  was completely the opposite. We wanted this goal  
and then also played for getting the equaliser.  We were close to get it, and that is why we really  
go home now and take a lot of positives from this  performance. Did you feel like that equaliser was  
going to come? You came so close. Eze was trying  and hit the post. It must have felt like it was  
just not happening for you. Yes, it felt the  same in the first half. So when I just sum up,  
I think with a big chance. So their first  goal is, we clear the ball and then they get  
the second shot. I do not know who, but the player  does not really hit the ball well. It falls to  
Isak and he also has no clinical finish, but  it bounces and is a goal. Then the second,  
we have a big chance with JP’s header, amazing  save from Woodman, and in the next situation  
Robertson hits the post and the ball is in. And  it was similar in the second half when we had our  
chances, our situations, and I think we kept  them on two finishes in the second half. And  
then the last, to be honest, was not  really a chance, but just shows also  
the quality, or the finishing quality, Liverpool  had today. That is what we have to accept. But  
the way we played, and not just how  many chances we created, so how little  
we gave to Liverpool. And I remember when we  won 1-0 here when I just arrived, I think it  
was 25 to 6 shots for Liverpool and the crossbar  and Dean Henderson, five, six incredible saves.  
And then we say, ah, what a game, because we won  1-0. I think today’s performance was much better,  
the way we played. I really liked how brave  we were in and out of possession. We had many  
very high, when we won the ball,  very high pressing situations,  
being brave, pressing them high, and also in  possession, we were really confident finding  
the right areas. But we have to accept that  the finishing was not good enough today.  
What was your perspective on the controversy  around your goal, your team’s goal? Obviously  
at the time Arne seemed pretty angry, fans were  angry. Did you feel like it was perfectly okay?  
No. That is why we also discussed. I discussed  with the fourth official, with Arne Slot,  
with Virgil van Dijk. So we watched it  back. It was so, let’s go from this side.  
If Ismaila Sarr hits his head, it is clear  the referee has to stop the game immediately.  
But I think the save was with his leg. Then the  ball goes to Daniel Muñoz. He tries to stand up,  
and in this moment I think Daniel Muñoz takes  the finish and the keeper raises his arm.  
He did not really see it, or it was more or less  at the same time, and then it was a goal. And  
I think the referee has to stop if he believes  it is a serious injury immediately, definitely.  
But we could see that the keeper could end the  game. And I just think that in these situations,  
to demand that the referee has to stop  can be very dangerous for the future,  
because we see in every set play the keeper is  involved in a duel. Let’s say he clears the ball  
with his arm and then just stays on the grass and  the referee stops. You never get a second phase,  
or you have one against the keeper. It is  always, when you get hit from four or five yards,  
it always hurts. And if he then just stays  on the grass and the referee has to stop,  
I think this would not be the best for football.  So that is why I think, at the end, it was,  
let’s say, not so clear, to be honest.  But I think it was the right decision.  
Did you ever consider sort of maybe thinking we  should let Liverpool score here? Was that ever  
something that you thought about in that moment?  We were discussing, to be honest. And I also said,  
for me it was clear, and this is what I told  the players. If the keeper has to get subbed,  
we would have definitely scored an own goal,  because then it was a serious injury and then  
it would have been wrong, I think. But in this  situation, again, he felt pain in this moment,  
but ask the keepers how often they feel pain  when they get hit from four or five yards. And  
also Daniel Muñoz, I think it was very parallel.  I say, you know, at the same time. So when  
the keeper raised his arm, Daniel Muñoz took the  finish. So that is why I think it was right. And  
yeah, okay. This gentleman here. So I was going  to ask about whether Van Dijk was asking you  
to let Liverpool score. No, no. He asked  me because nobody really on the pitch, and  
everything goes so quick. For us it is easy, or  especially in the stand, you see everything from  
like a bird’s-eye perspective. We watched it  back on the video, and I told him that it was  
more or less the finish. He saw that  the goalkeeper already raised his arm  
and gave the signal that he cannot continue  playing, and then Daniel Muñoz took the finish.  
And I explained to him that it was more or less  at the same time, and I think he did not see it.  
Okay, Bobby. Can I just check, Tyrick, is that  tactical? No, no. Tyrick felt his Achilles,  
to be honest. It is not just since today,  so it is an ongoing issue here. Our medical  
department is treating it very well, and today  then he said he cannot continue. And also,  
I think Borna Sosa also did really well. Did not  play for many, for many weeks now, and did very  
well, like all the other subs, I think, did like  in the last games. Always did a good impact, yeah.  
And it is just, we missed the final margin to  get the equaliser at the end. Do you think he  
can be managed in time for Thursday? I think so,  yes. Okay. Any others? No. That is a lot. Cheers.
title: GLASNER: “IT WOULDNT BE THE BEST FOR FOOTBALL!”  Liverpool 3-1 Crystal Palace
